coordinates.note: No official ARIANNA page, technical paper, or geodetic source fetched this session gives a numeric latitude/longitude for the Moore's Bay station field; the prototype (2010) and testbed (2019) arXiv papers describe the location only qualitatively ('Moore's Bay on the Ross Ice Shelf'). The coordinate used here is Minna Bluff, a named headland near Moore's Bay, taken from Wikipedia (rank 12) as a coarse regional pointer only. `kind` is set to 'campus' (the validator's A23 exception path: a site holding a detector needs a 'detector'/'underground_lab' marker unless it is 'campus' with confidence approximate/uncertain and a note) rather than 'detector', precisely because this is not a surveyed station position.

depth.note: This is the Ross Ice Shelf thickness at the prototype deployment point, not a detector burial depth (ARIANNA stations sit on/near the ice surface).
depth.quote: The ice shelf thickness was measured to be 572 +/- 6 m at the deployment site.

summary.plain: A patch of the vast floating Ross Ice Shelf in Antarctica, more than half a kilometre thick, where a small array of surface radio antennas once listened for neutrinos.
summary.technical: Moore's Bay station field on the Ross Ice Shelf, Antarctica; ice shelf thickness measured at 572±6 m at the original 2009 prototype deployment point. No surveyed lat/lon for the array found this session; coordinates recorded only as a coarse regional pointer.
